facts.text: The Initial Order was granted 1 February 2021, appointing E&Y as Monitor with a 10-day stay period.
facts.quote: On February 1, 2021, the Court granted an initial order (the "Initial Order") that, among other things, appointed Ernst & Young Inc. as monitor of the Applicant in these CCAA proceedings … and approved a stay of proceedings for the initial 10-day period

facts.text: The comeback motion was scheduled for 9:00am on 10 February 2021.
facts.quote: The Court scheduled a comeback motion for 9:00am on February 10, 2021

facts.text: The Administration Charge, Directors' Charge and DIP Lender's Charge are to rank in priority to ALL other secured creditors as defined in the CCAA.
facts.quote: the granting of the Administration Charge, the Directors' Charge and the DIP Lender's Charge in priority to all other "secured creditors" as defined in the CCAA

facts.text: The Stay Period, set to expire 11 February 2021, is to be extended to 30 April 2021.
facts.quote: The Stay Period is currently set to expire on February 11, 2021. The Applicant requests an extension of the Stay Period up to and including April 30, 2021.

facts.text: Justice Sean Dunphy of the Ontario Superior Court of Justice was appointed Court-Appointed Mediator. The Court proposed him; all parties confirmed no objection.
facts.quote: the Court proposed to appoint the Honourable Justice Sean Dunphy of the Ontario Superior Court of Justice as the Court-Appointed Mediator … All parties at the case conference confirmed that there were no objections to Justice Dunphy's appointment as mediator.

facts.text: Dunphy was previously a leading insolvency lawyer with CCAA and complex labour experience, and is bilingual.
facts.quote: During his career, Justice Dunphy was a leading insolvency lawyer with extensive experience in CCAA restructurings, including complex labour negotiations, and is bilingual.

facts.text: LU approached FOUR external lenders specializing in real-estate and infrastructure lending; three submitted non-binding draft term sheets; two were shortlisted; one term sheet was executed.
facts.quote: These discussions resulted in the Applicant receiving non-binding draft term sheets from three potential lenders … determined that of the three initial proposals, two were sufficiently preferable to merit narrowing ongoing negotiations to these two parties.

facts.text: LU executed the DIP Term Sheet with Firm Capital Corporation, which then ASSIGNED its interest to Firm Capital Mortgage Fund Inc. — the entity that is the actual DIP Lender.
facts.quote: the Applicant executed a term sheet (the "DIP Term Sheet") with Firm Capital Corporation. Subsequent to the execution of the DIP Term Sheet, Firm Capital Corporation assigned its interest to Firm Capital Mortgage Fund Inc. (the "DIP Lender").

facts.text: DIP facility: secured, non-revolving, maximum principal $25 million, maturity 1 May 2021, extendable by 90 days on milestones.
facts.quote: the maximum principal amount is $25 million with a maturity date of May 1, 2021. The maturity date may be extended for an additional 90 days if LU achieves the following milestones

facts.text: DIP interest: the greater of 8.50% per annum or the TD Canada Trust posted prime rate plus 6.05% per annum, compounded and payable monthly in arrears.
facts.quote: at a rate that is the greater of 8.50% per annum or the TD Canada Trust Posted Bank Prime Rate of Interest from time to time plus 6.05% per annum

facts.text: The DIP extension milestones are judged by the DIP Lender "in its sole and unfettered discretion" — including whether LU is financially sustainable.
facts.quote: to the satisfaction of the DIP Lender in its sole and unfettered discretion

facts.text: The milestones require LU to reach consensus on academic restructuring, to settle with LUFA (terminations, grievances, a new collective agreement), and to deliver a multi-year budget showing sustainability.
facts.quote: LU enters into a negotiated settlement with LUFA with respect to terminations to be effected, resolution of outstanding grievances, and the terms of a new collective agreement

facts.text: TWO parties expressed interest in submitting COMPETING DIP proposals (a law firm on 4 Feb 2021 and another party on 5 Feb 2021). LU DECLINED both.
facts.quote: the Applicant determined that given the number of weeks it took other potential lenders to conduct their due diligence … it was highly unlikely that a new party could negotiate and execute a non-disclosure agreement, conduct its due diligence and be in a position to submit a binding offer … Accordingly, the Applicant declined the request from the law firm to proceed with any due diligence process

facts.text: The Monitor repeats the reliability caveat: LU's Finance department "has experienced certain challenges as a result of its limited team and resources", so the Information may be limited.
facts.quote: Dr. Haché Notes that he has relied upon information provided by LU's Finance department which has experienced certain challenges as a result of its limited team and resources. As a result, the Monitor notes that the Information relied upon for purposes of this First Report may be limited by these challenges.

facts.text: LU launched stakeholder websites at laurentianu.info and ulaurentienne.info, and implemented new fiscal restraint policies authorizing only necessary expenses.
facts.quote: the Applicant has drafted and implemented new fiscal restraint policies to monitor and authorize only necessary expenses during the pendency of this CCAA proceeding.

facts.text: Classes continued virtually with no disruption following the Initial Order.
facts.quote: Student classes are continuing (virtually due to the Pandemic) with no disruption.

must_not_miss.text: Firm Capital Corporation executed the term sheet, then ASSIGNED its interest to Firm Capital Mortgage Fund Inc., which is the actual DIP Lender. These are two distinct entities.
must_not_miss.why: Document 3 names only "Firm Capital Corporation". An extractor that collapses these into one entity has lost the assignment; one that creates two unlinked entities has lost the relationship. Both failure modes are worth catching, and this is the only place the distinction is stated.

must_not_miss.text: LU declined TWO expressions of interest in competing DIP financing, received 4 and 5 February 2021, days before the comeback motion.
must_not_miss.why: The insolvent institution turned away potential competing lenders while locked into an 8.5% facility with a $500K fee. The paragraph reads as procedural housekeeping and is easy to skim.

must_not_miss.text: The DIP extension milestones rest on the lender's "sole and unfettered discretion" — the phrase appears twice, including on the question of whether LU is financially sustainable.
must_not_miss.why: A private lender holds unilateral judgment over whether a public university continues. Buried in sub-sub-clauses.

must_not_miss.text: The Administration Charge triples ($400K → $1.25M) and the Directors' Charge more than doubles ($2M → $5M), all ranking ahead of every other secured creditor.
must_not_miss.why: $6.25M of super-priority charges jumping the queue ahead of existing secured lenders, listed as roman-numeral sub-items on page 2 in a purpose statement.

must_not_miss.text: Justice Sean Dunphy — the mediator — was himself a leading insolvency lawyer before the bench, and the Court proposed him rather than the parties.
must_not_miss.why: The mediator's identity and provenance, given once. Note also that bilingualism was added as a criterion here that was NOT in the Pre-Filing Report's list — a small drift worth catching.

must_not_miss.text: The Monitor's reliability caveat about LU's Finance department, repeated from the Pre-Filing Report — including the same erroneous affidavit date ("sworn January 30, 2020").
must_not_miss.why: Buried in disclaimer boilerplate. The repetition of the date error across two documents is itself a fact: it is a copy-paste, not a fresh statement.

must_not_miss.text: The DIP process ran under two successive NDAs, with LU's identity withheld until the first was signed.
must_not_miss.why: How an insolvent public university shopped for money in secret. Procedural, and routinely dropped.

X.summary:
This First Monitor’s Report for the Laurentian University CCAA proceeding exists to update the court and stakeholders on the university’s restructuring, the stay of proceedings, and the monitor’s requests for extensions and financing in the file opened as Laurentian University of Sudbury’s court-supervised restructuring. Laurentian commenced CCAA proceedings on 2021-02-01 in Ontario Superior Court of Justice file CV-21-656040-00CL, Ernst & Young Inc. was appointed monitor the same day, and the initial stay ran to 2021-02-11 while the university continued virtual classes and the monitor set up creditor communications, notices, and a case website.

The report supports extending the stay to 2021-04-30, appointing Justice Sean Dunphy as mediator, approving up to $25 million of secured DIP financing from Firm Capital Mortgage Fund Inc., and increasing the administration and directors’ charges. The proposed financing carries interest at the greater of 8.50% or TD prime plus 6.05%, a $500,000 commitment fee, and a possible 90-day extension if Laurentian reaches stakeholder consensus on academic restructuring, settles with LUFA, and produces a satisfactory revised cash flow forecast and multiyear budget.

Material restructuring issues include academic and headcount changes, the federated universities model, and a new collective agreement with LUFA, all under a mediation confidentiality protocol that makes mediation communications generally without prejudice and inadmissible. The report also flags Laurentian’s pension and benefit pressures, including a DB pension plan solvency ratio of 85.4% and about a $4.5 million going-concern deficiency, monthly payroll of about $11 million, and monthly DB pension contributions of about $1.2 million, while noting that the university’s secured creditors are mainly subcontractors with construction liens and limited equipment lessors.

key_facts.fact: Laurentian University approached four external lenders about DIP financing and used NDAs and a virtual data room before sharing its financial circumstances.
key_facts.quote: LU, through its legal counsel, approached four external lenders that specialize in real estate and infrastructure based lending, including DIP financing.

key_facts.fact: Firm Capital Corporation executed the DIP term sheet, then assigned its interest to Firm Capital Mortgage Fund Inc., which became the DIP lender.
key_facts.quote: the Applicant executed a term sheet... with Firm Capital Corporation. Subsequent to the execution of the DIP Term Sheet, Firm Capital Corporation assigned its interest to Firm Capital Mortgage Fund Inc. (the 'DIP Lender').

key_facts.quote: the maximum principal amount is $25 million with a maturity date of May 1, 2021.

key_facts.quote: The maturity date may be extended for an additional 90 days if LU achieves the following milestones...

key_facts.fact: The monitor recorded late interest from other prospective DIP proposals, but the applicant declined further diligence because a binding alternative could not likely be completed before the comeback motion.
key_facts.quote: the Applicant declined the request from the law firm to proceed with any due diligence process and the Monitor communicated the same message to the other party.

key_facts.fact: The applicant sought to extend the stay period from 2021-02-11 to 2021-04-30.
key_facts.quote: The Stay Period is currently set to expire on February 11, 2021. The Applicant requests an extension of the Stay Period up to and including April 30, 2021.

key_facts.quote: the Applicant administers three employee pension and benefit plans: (a) a registered defined benefit pension plan... (b) a supplementary unfunded retirement plan... and (c) a retirement health benefits plan.

key_facts.quote: The proposed facility is assumed to be advanced in two tranches in accordance with the terms of the DIP Term Sheet.

key_facts.quote: on February 1, 2021, the Applicant commenced court-supervised restructuring proceedings... Ernst & Young Inc. was appointed as monitor of the Applicant.

key_facts.quote: The Initial Order grants... a stay of proceedings up to and including February 11, 2021... No claims procedure has yet been submitted to or approved by the Court.

key_facts.fact: Laurentian University of Sudbury commenced CCAA proceedings on February 1, 2021 under Court File No. CV-21-656040-00CL.
key_facts.quote: the Applicant commenced court-supervised restructuring proceedings (the 'CCAA Proceedings') under the CCAA.

key_facts.quote: the Initial Order directs Laurentian University to make no payments of principal, interest or otherwise on account of amounts owing by the Applicant to its creditors as of February 1, 2021.

Y.summary: This is the First Report of Ernst & Young Inc. (Monitor) filed February 7, 2021 in the CCAA proceedings of Laurentian University of Sudbury (Court File No. CV-21-656040-00CL), prepared for the comeback motion scheduled February 10, 2021. The report covers LU's operational status since the February 1, 2021 Initial Order, the appointment of Justice Sean Dunphy as Court-Appointed Mediator, a request to extend the stay period to April 30, 2021, and the terms of a $25 million DIP financing facility with Firm Capital Mortgage Fund Inc. The Monitor also seeks court approval of an Amended and Restated Initial Order that would increase the Administration Charge to $1.25 million, increase the Directors' Charge to $5 million, stay special payments to the DB Pension Plan, and stay FIPPA information requests. The cash flow forecast projects total receipts of approximately $29.5 million and total disbursements of approximately $58.6 million over the 13-week period ending April 30, 2021, with the shortfall funded by DIP draws totalling approximately $24 million.

key_facts.fact: Laurentian University of Sudbury filed a CCAA application before the Ontario Superior Court of Justice (Commercial List) on February 1, 2021, seeking a stay of proceedings to allow financial and operational restructuring.
key_facts.quote: Laurentian University of Sudbury ('LU' or the 'Applicant') brought an application (the 'CCAA Application') before this Court seeking an initial order pursuant to the Companies' Creditors Arrangement Act

key_facts.fact: The court granted the Initial Order on February 1, 2021, appointing Ernst & Young Inc. as Monitor and granting an initial 10-day stay of proceedings expiring February 11, 2021.
A comeback motion was scheduled for 9:00 am on February 10, 2021.
LU was incorporated on March 28, 1960, under An Act to Incorporate Laurentian University of Sudbury, S.O. 1960, c. 151.
LU is a publicly funded, bilingual and tricultural post-secondary institution located in the City of Greater Sudbury, Ontario, and is one of the largest employers in Sudbury.
LU is a non-share capital corporation and a registered charity exempt from income tax under Section 149 of the Income Tax Act.

The Affidavit of Dr. Robert Haché (sworn January 30, 2021) — the Initial Order Affidavit — notes that LU's Finance department has experienced challenges due to its limited team and resources, which may limit the reliability of financial information.
The Monitor participated in a call with the Applicant and the Ministry of Colleges and Universities (MCU) since the granting of the Initial Order.

On February 4, 2021, the Monitor sent a Notice to Creditors by prepaid ordinary mail to all known creditors with claims exceeding $1,000, and published the notice in the Globe and Mail (National Edition) and the Sudbury Star.
On February 4, 2021, the Monitor posted a list of Known Creditors and amounts owing per LU's books and records on the Monitor's Website.
A case conference regarding the appointment of a Court-Appointed Mediator was held on February 5, 2021, attended by the Monitor, counsel to LU, and counsel to LUFA.
Chief Justice Morawetz appointed Justice Sean Dunphy of the Ontario Superior Court of Justice as Court-Appointed Mediator on February 5, 2021; all parties confirmed no objections to his appointment.

Justice Dunphy's mandate as Court-Appointed Mediator covers: restructuring of academic programs, restructuring of faculty, a new collective agreement with LUFA (including resolution of outstanding grievances), restructuring of the Federated Universities model, and the framework for LU's future operations.

LU approached four external lenders specializing in real estate and infrastructure-based lending for DIP financing; three submitted non-binding draft term sheets and two were shortlisted after initial review.
LU executed a DIP Term Sheet with Firm Capital Corporation, which subsequently assigned its interest to Firm Capital Mortgage Fund Inc. as the DIP Lender.

The DIP facility is a secured non-revolving credit facility with a maximum principal amount of $25 million and a maturity date of May 1, 2021, extendable by 90 days if LU meets specified restructuring milestones to the DIP Lender's satisfaction.
DIP interest accrues at the greater of 8.50% per annum or TD Canada Trust Posted Bank Prime Rate plus 6.05% per annum, compounded and payable monthly in arrears.
A commitment fee of $500,000 is deemed fully earned and payable to the DIP Lender upon court approval of the Amended and Restated Initial Order approving the DIP financing.

On February 4, 2021 and February 5, 2021, third parties contacted LU's counsel and the Monitor expressing interest in submitting competing DIP proposals; LU declined to allow further due diligence given the timeline and the already-executed DIP Term Sheet.
The stay period is set to expire February 11, 2021; the Applicant requests an extension to April 30, 2021.

LU administers three employee pension and benefit plans: (a) a registered defined benefit pension plan (DB Pension Plan); (b) a supplementary unfunded retirement plan (SuRP); and (c) a retirement health benefits plan (RHBP).

The most recent actuarial valuation of the DB Pension Plan (as of January 1, 2020, updated December 2020) showed a solvency ratio of 85.4% and a going concern deficiency of approximately $4.5 million, to be addressed over up to ten years beginning January 1, 2021.

DB Pension Plan current service contributions for the next three years were set at $16,188,000 annually (approximately $1,349,000 per month); an annual special payment contribution of $505,000 (approximately $42,083 per month) is also required to address the going concern deficiency.
The Amended and Restated Initial Order requests a stay of pre-filing and post-filing special payments to the DB Pension Plan to assist LU's liquidity.
The SuRP and RHBP are unfunded contractual obligations to former or retired employees; the Initial Order stays amounts payable under these plans.
The proposed Amended and Restated Initial Order also requests a stay of existing, pending, and future FIPPA information requests to LU.

The proposed super-priority charges in rank order are: (1) Administration Charge up to $1.25 million; (2) Directors' Charge up to $2 million; (3) DIP Lender's Charge up to $25 million; (4) additional Directors' Charge up to $3 million (total Directors' Charge $5 million).
LU's secured creditors are primarily subcontractors with registered construction liens against LU's real property and limited equipment lessors.

The Administration Charge (up to $1.25 million) covers professional fees of counsel and advisors to the Applicant, the Monitor, the Monitor's independent counsel, and independent counsel to the Board.
LU's aggregate monthly payroll is approximately $11 million; monthly DB Pension Plan contributions are approximately $1.2 million; and vacation pay accrues at approximately $800,000 per month.

The 13-week cash flow forecast (January 30 to April 30, 2021) projects total receipts of $29,514,000 and total disbursements of $58,553,000, with a net cash shortfall of approximately $29,039,000 before DIP draws.
The cash flow forecast projects total payroll and benefits disbursements of approximately $31,310,000 and total pension contributions of approximately $4,322,000 over the 13-week period.
The forecast projects total operating grants of $21,406,000 over the 13-week period, funded semi-monthly by the Province of Ontario.
The Endowment Fund has a beginning balance of $55,736,000 in the cash flow forecast, with no transfers in or out during the period except a projected market-value change of negative $860,000.
The Monitor's report was signed by Sharon S. Hamilton, CPA, CA, CIRP, LIT, Senior Vice President of Ernst & Young Inc.
Thornton Grout Finnigan LLP acted as lawyers for the Applicant in the mediator appointment order, with D.J. Miller, Mitchell W. Grossell, Andrew Hanrahan, and Derek Harland listed as counsel.
Counsel appearing for LUFA at the February 5, 2021 case conference included Charles Sinclair, Susan Philpott, and David Wright; Ashley Taylor and Ben Muller appeared for the Monitor.
Michael Kennedy acted as Labour Counsel for the Applicant at the February 5, 2021 case conference.

(assigned from Firm Capital Corporation) at a minimum 8.50% annual interest rate with a $500,000 commitment fee, an extension of the stay of proceedings to April 30, 2021, increases to the Administration Charge (to $1.25 million) and Directors' Charge (to $5 million total), a stay of special payments to the defined benefit pension plan, and a stay of FIPPA requests.
